paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God sends you, no lock, no council and no threat gets the last word. The apostles got arrested, and an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors and told them to go tell the people "the full message of this new life" (Acts 5:19-20). Then they stood in front of the same people who locked them up and said, "We must obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29). That's not stubbornness, baker. That's knowing who they answer to.

Now look at Gamaliel, the Pharisee and teacher of the law. He tells the Council that if this is of human origin it will fail, but if it is from God, "you will not be able to stop them" (Acts 5:38-39). I think that line is bigger than he knew. Human plans come and go, and God's work keeps standing, so you don't have to hold the whole thing up with your own two hands.

And the apostles? They got flogged, and they left "rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name" (Acts 5:41). Then they went right back to teaching every day, in the temple courts and from house to house (Acts 5:42). Baker, I spent years in a drawer wondering if I mattered, and then God reached in and put me to work. If He can do that for a worn-out stamper, you can trust Him with whatever He's asking of you today.
